answer: Ladders are permitted in the orchard only when a second worker holds the base of the ladder. [Doc_07 §2.1] Ladders are not permitted in the orchard overnight. [Doc_07 §2.2] Ladders must be returned to the tool shed. [Doc_07 §2.2]

judged_claims.text: Ladders are permitted in the orchard only when a second worker holds the base of the ladder.
Ladders are not permitted in the orchard overnight.
Ladders must be returned to the tool shed.

query: Sorry, I meant crates instead of ladders.

claims.text: A picker may fill at most 40 crates per shift.

answer: A picker may fill at most 40 crates per shift. [Doc_07 §3] Damaged fruit is placed in the compost bin, not in the crates. [Doc_07 §3] The harvest supervisor checks the crate count at the end of every shift. [Doc_07 §3] Crates are stacked no more than five high. [Doc_07 §3]

judged_claims.text: A picker may fill at most 40 crates per shift.
Damaged fruit is placed in the compost bin, not in the crates.
The harvest supervisor checks the crate count at the end of every shift.
Crates are stacked no more than five high.

query: How is the lens polished?

claims.text: The keeper polishes the lens with a dry chamois cloth.

answer: The keeper polishes the lens with a dry chamois cloth. [fixture_lighthouse_manual §1.2] Abrasive powders are not permitted on the lens. [fixture_lighthouse_manual §1.2]

judged_claims.text: The keeper polishes the lens with a dry chamois cloth.
Abrasive powders are not permitted on the lens.

query: Actually, I meant the wick.

claims.text: Wicks are trimmed to a height of 4 millimetres.

answer: Wicks are trimmed to a height of 4 millimetres. [fixture_lighthouse_manual §1.1] A wick trimmed too short produces a dim beam. [fixture_lighthouse_manual §1.1] A wick left too long produces soot on the lens. [fixture_lighthouse_manual §1.1]

judged_claims.text: Wicks are trimmed to a height of 4 millimetres.
A wick trimmed too short produces a dim beam.
A wick left too long produces soot on the lens.
